answer_sql:
WITH o AS (
  SELECT
    order_key,
    MIN(customer_key) AS customer_key,
    MIN(store_key) AS store_key,
    SUM(net_amount) AS order_net
  FROM contoso_served.v_contoso5_sales_line
  GROUP BY
    order_key
), t AS (
  SELECT
    o.order_net,
    s.country_code AS store_cc,
    c.country_code AS cust_cc
  FROM o
  JOIN contoso_served.dim_store AS s
    ON o.store_key = s.store_key
  JOIN contoso_served.dim_customer AS c
    ON o.customer_key = c.customer_key
)
SELECT
  dc.country_name AS country,
  ROUND(AVG(t.order_net) FILTER(WHERE
    t.cust_cc = dc.country_code), 2) AS avg_order_value_customer_country,
  ROUND(AVG(t.order_net) FILTER(WHERE
    t.store_cc = dc.country_code), 2) AS avg_order_value_store_country
FROM contoso_served.dim_country AS dc
CROSS JOIN t
WHERE
  dc.country_code <> '--'
GROUP BY
  1
ORDER BY
  avg_order_value_customer_country DESC

sections.title: What it says its rows are

body.value: Eight rows, one per country Contoso sells in, each holding two versions of one quantity: the average value of a single order placed there, where an order's value is the money actually charged across all its lines after discount, and the average is taken over orders — 93,470 of them — rather than over the 223,974 lines or over customers. The first figure attributes each order to the country its buyer lives in and covers every order on record; the second attributes it to the country the selling shop stood in and covers 54,502, every internet order having fallen out for want of a country. Both span the full ten years of trading, 2016-05-18 to 2025-12-31. The returned rows match the figures I claimed before seeing them, to the penny, and the store column descends in the same sequence as the customer column, which is what makes the ranking claim safe. WHAT IS NOT IN THESE FIGURES: no tax and no shipping, because the warehouse holds neither; no exclusion of cancelled, returned or refunded orders, because no column in this bundle records an order's status; no `--` sentinel row, which under the store reading would otherwise stand as a ninth and second-largest "country" named Online; and no currency conversion, the amounts being USD already whatever currency a sale was transacted in.

value:
Which country do you mean — where the customer lives, or where the shop that took the order stood? There is no country written on an order itself, so one can only be reached by choosing, and the choice decides whether 38,968 internet orders are in the answer or absent from it.

IF YOU MEAN WHERE THE CUSTOMER LIVES — all 93,470 orders counted, internet included (average order value, net, USD):
Italy 2,459.71 · United Kingdom 2,413.06 · United States 2,356.13 · Germany 2,319.60 · Canada 2,307.13 · Australia 2,288.96 · France 2,250.41 · Netherlands 2,204.90

IF YOU MEAN WHERE THE SHOP STOOD — only the 54,502 orders rung up in a physical shop; the 38,968 web-shop orders (86,790,054.13 USD) belong to no country and drop out entirely:
Italy 2,617.62 · United Kingdom 2,498.53 · United States 2,430.24 · Germany 2,427.47 · Canada 2,396.95 · Australia 2,348.50 · France 2,272.68 · Netherlands 2,239.53

WHAT THE CHOICE DOES NOT CHANGE: the league table. Both readings give the same eight countries in the same order — Italy highest, Netherlands lowest, United States third either way. Every store figure is simply higher than its customer counterpart, by 22.27 (France) to 157.91 (Italy), because the internet orders the store reading omits are cheaper on average (2,227.21) than shop orders. So if you want to know WHERE ORDERS ARE BIGGEST, you have your answer already and need not choose. If you want to quote a FIGURE, you must.

ONE PLACE THE CHOICE BITES HARDER: the United States and Germany sit 36.53 apart under the customer reading but 2.77 apart under the store reading — effectively tied. Do not call that gap real without saying which reading produced it.

Two populations, because I declined to collapse them into one. COMMON TO BOTH: all 93,470 distinct orders, collapsed from 223,974 sales lines by order_key per Order's declared grounding; the full extent of order_date, 2016-05-18 to 2025-12-31, because the question named no period (order.default.an_unscoped_question_covers_all_time, confidence C); both sales channels, because the subject here is a money measure and store.resolution.the_channel_is_the_location_sentinel scopes its `physical` default to questions whose subject is a store; no order-status exclusion, because none is expressible in this bundle; and reporting over the 8 real country codes only, `--` excluded per country.exclusion.sentinel_is_not_a_country. THE CUSTOMER-COUNTRY COLUMN is computed over all 93,470 of those orders. THE STORE-COUNTRY COLUMN is computed over 54,502 — the 38,968 web-shop orders carry `--` as their store country and are therefore absent, which is a consequence of that reading rather than a filter I applied.

Each row also carries the one customer who placed it, the one store or web shop that took it, and the one day it was placed — measured just now, no order spans two customers, two stores or two dates, so each of those is a single fact about the order and not a choice between several.

WITH o AS (
  SELECT
    order_key,
    MIN(customer_key) AS customer_key,
    MIN(store_key) AS store_key,
    SUM(net_amount) AS order_net
  FROM contoso_served.v_contoso5_sales_line
  GROUP BY
    order_key
), t AS (
  SELECT
    o.order_key,
    o.order_net,
    s.country_code AS store_cc,
    l.country_code AS loc_cc,
    c.country_code AS cust_cc
  FROM o
  JOIN contoso_served.dim_store AS s
    ON o.store_key = s.store_key
  JOIN contoso_served.dim_location AS l
    ON s.location_code = l.location_code
  JOIN contoso_served.dim_customer AS c
    ON o.customer_key = c.customer_key
), r AS (
  SELECT
    'store' AS reading,
    store_cc AS cc,
    order_net
  FROM t
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    'location',
    loc_cc,
    order_net
  FROM t
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    'customer',
    cust_cc,
    order_net
  FROM t
)
SELECT
  r.reading,
  r.cc AS country_code,
  dc.country_name,
  COUNT(*) AS orders,
  ROUND(AVG(r.order_net), 2) AS avg_order_value,
  ROUND(SUM(r.order_net), 2) AS net_revenue
FROM r
LEFT JOIN contoso_served.dim_country AS dc
  ON r.cc = dc.country_code
GROUP BY
  1,
  2,
  3
ORDER BY
  r.reading,
  avg_order_value DESC

), t AS (

    o.order_net,

  dc.country_code <> '--'

value.means: Eight rows, one per country Contoso sells in, each holding two versions of one quantity: the average value of a single order placed there, where an order's value is the money actually charged across all its lines after discount, and the average is taken over orders — 93,470 of them — rather than over the 223,974 lines or over customers. The first figure attributes each order to the country its buyer lives in and covers every order on record; the second attributes it to the country the selling shop stood in and covers 54,502, every internet order having fallen out for want of a country. Both span the full ten years of trading, 2016-05-18 to 2025-12-31. The returned rows match the figures I claimed before seeing them, to the penny, and the store column descends in the same sequence as the customer column, which is what makes the ranking claim safe. WHAT IS NOT IN THESE FIGURES: no tax and no shipping, because the warehouse holds neither; no exclusion of cancelled, returned or refunded orders, because no column in this bundle records an order's status; no `--` sentinel row, which under the store reading would otherwise stand as a ninth and second-largest "country" named Online; and no currency conversion, the amounts being USD already whatever currency a sale was transacted in.
